title: Intriguing topological superconductor phases in long-range extended Kitaev models: an interplay between sub-lattices and power-law interaction
authors: Dharana Joshi, Amaan Khan, Tanay Nag
abstract: The power-law profile of hopping and superconductivity introduces rich critical phenomena that are not possible to explore in the nearest-neighbor models. Having this in mind, we construct the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH)-Kitaev model with mono-, bi-, and tri-partite sub-lattices where superconductivity [hopping] is of power-law Kitaev [SSH] type. The long-range (LR) superconductivity can alone gap out the zero-momentum critical line while LR hopping alters the finite-momentum critical line. There exists open-ended critical line at vanishing superconducting gap on the phase diagram for all versions of the SSH-Kitaev model. Interestingly, LR superconductivity (hopping) promotes massive Dirac (Majorana zero) modes, while in a finite-size system, their emergence in open boundary conditions is caused by the bulk gap of the anti-periodic Hamiltonian in momentum space. This indicates an unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence for power-law models as compared to what is seen in the short-range models. Importantly, the thermodynamic phase boundaries are correctly reproduced by the above unconventional correspondence. Intriguingly, an even (odd) number of sub-lattices yields an integer (half-integer) winding number while the massive Dirac modes continue to survive irrespective of the sub-lattice profile as long as there exists LR pairing only.
summary: This work explores topological superconductivity in extended Kitaev models by introducing power-law interactions and multiple sub-lattices. The authors demonstrate that long-range pairing and hopping induce unique topological features, leading to an unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence. This provides deeper insight into how dimensionality and interaction decay affect Majorana zero mode physics.
main_problem: The study investigates topological superconducting phases in extended Kitaev models that incorporate long-range (LR) hopping and superconductivity, focusing on the role of sub-lattices and power-law interactions.
main_result: The model exhibits unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence, where LR superconductivity promotes massive Dirac (Majorana zero) modes, and the winding number can take half-integer values depending on the sub-lattice parity.
method: The analysis involves constructing generalized SSH-Kitaev models and calculating topological invariants, such as the winding number, in both the thermodynamic limit and for finite-size systems.
model_or_system: The system is based on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH)-Kitaev model, extended to include mono-, bi-, and tri-partite sub-lattices. The Hamiltonian features power-law decay ($r^{-\epsilon}, r^{-\alpha}$) for both hopping and superconducting pairing terms.
key_observables: Topological invariants (winding number $W_r$), Mid-Gap Modes (MDMs), and the existence/location of critical lines.
important_parameters: Power-law decay exponents ($\alpha, \epsilon$), chemical potential ($\mu$), and the number of sub-lattices (even vs. odd).
main_assumptions: The analysis compares results from the thermodynamic limit (momentum space) to finite-size systems (real space), noting discrepancies in the boundary correspondence.
figures_summary: Figures schematically represent the three SSH-Kitaev models and show winding number phase diagrams illustrating how superconducting/hopping conditions alter the topological phase boundaries.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the SSH-Kitaev model across different sub-lattice structures (SSH1, SSH2, SSH3), comparing the effects of LR hopping versus LR superconductivity on the topological phase diagram and the resulting boundary conditions.
why_interesting: The findings on unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence and the persistence of Majorana modes despite changes in the winding number are highly relevant for understanding topological superconductivity in engineered quantum materials.

In (a), J (∆) represents hopping (superconducting pairing) term, designated by black (red) color, and ϵ (α) denotes hopping (superconducting) power-law exponent. In (b), V is intra-cell hopping, W1 and W2 are inter-cell hopping. In (c), V1 and V2 are intra-cell hopping, and W is inter-cell hopping.
